full_judgment:
4. Mr MA Samad, the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners, submits that as the proceeding in Money Suit was stayed from 27-3-88 to 18-5-2000, the plaintiffs in view of Article 110 of the Limitation Act was entitled to add further claims of damages of Taka 71, 00,000 and the application for amendment was not barred on the date of making the application. 

 8. Mr Samad bases his case on Article 110 of the Limitation Act. Article 110 prescribes a period of three years for a suit for arrears, when it becomes due. There is generally no limitation for an amendment of the pleading provided the claim sought to be added by such amendment is not barred on the date of institution of the suit or on the date of such application. 

 9. In the case of Nuran Nahar vs Mohd Fazlur Rahman, the suit was for recovery of a car. On 12-5-73 the suit was instituted. On 18-12-75 the plaintiff made an application for amendment of the plaint for adding a prayer for compensation for unauthorised retention of the case. The trial Court having allowed the prayer on 8-1-76 and this Division having affirmed the decision of the trial Court, the defendant took leave on the ground of limitation. 

 11. In the case of JM Andrews vs Radio Engineering Co, AIR 1963 Mysore 113, the phrase "as and when the arrears become due" of Article 110 of the Limitation Act in a suit for arrears was considered. The plaintiff on 8-12-49 made an application before the Rent Controller for fixation of rate. Rent Controller rejected the application and, on appeal, the appellate Court by its order dated 30-9-53 fixed the rate of rent by enhancement at Taka 75 per month with effect from the date of application. 

 13. In the case of Attaullah Malik, vs Rashid and others, on 20-10-61 a suit was instituted for arrears of the period from 15-12-50 to 14-10-61. The issue was as to whether the claim for rents for more than three years was barred by limitation under article 110 of the Limitation Act. The word 'due' received close attention of the Bench. It held, 

 "Our conclusion from what was been discussed above is that the word 'due' in article 110 of the Limitation Act means the date on which the cause of action arises for filing a suit and, in this context, the rent for the entire period of 10 years and 10 months became due on 19th November, 1960 when the Custodian upheld the order of the Additional Custodian (Judicial) and the respondents were, in law, entitled to sue for the recovery of the arrears of rent." 

 15. Firstly, the limitation begins to run or stops running by operation of law. It is not the intention of the legislature that one can get the limitation stopped running and again should restart running at one's sweet wish. In view of Title Appeal No. 84 of 1988, on 27-3-88 the plaintiffs got further proceedings in their money suit No. 1 of 1986 stayed till disposal of said appeal. With the disposal of the appeal, the stay expired automatically, for which no order was necessary, just to bring it to the notice of the court. What the plaintiffs did only on 26-4-2000 by making an application. Upon the application, the court by its order dated 18-5-2000 recalled its order of stay.
